text: Hey everyone I'm wondering if there's any useful/helpful list of apps, companies, or resources in general that avoid AI (they don't have to be vocally or openly "anti", but at least explicitly avoid it) that you know of? I'm not looking to start a discussion on what's good/bad or (un)worthy about AI, or who's for/against, just links and/or communities promoting this sentiment/position. For example, https://www.rebeltechalliance.org would be one of those resources. Thank you! https://codeberg.org/ethical-foss/ai-free-foss-alternatives Thanks, I wasn't aware of this list, though it shows very few alternatives (and I'm not saying they exist, but it almost makes it seem more helpless). It also links to other resources but I think https://noai.starlightnet.work/list.html could be mainly what you're looking for. It's such a shame that a list titled "AI-free FOSS Alternatives" ends up becoming the opposite of its stated goal, with the top level section being "Tainted Software" and occasional sporadic little notes listing alternatives. I like the steadfast anti-AI people even though I'm not really one of them, and I want them to thrive and carve out a lasting space online. Putting more focus on the positives of the anti-AI vision and way less on the rejection and refusal stuff would probably help with that, and I think this is a really clear example where the negative side of the message has stolen the show unnecessarily. The "tainted" list is inside baseball stuff and belongs in the equivalent of a Wikipedia talk page on there. https://noailist.org/ Similar to the rebel tech alliance, there's the trustworthy technology group. They have a Zulip chat you could join to discuss this further. The "No AI" Webring is related - https://baccyflap.com/noai/ Thanks, my blog is a part of it! 😊 Well, I work there, but we are both a FOSS nonprofit and also have a firm no-gen-AI policy at the Spritely Institute , and do pretty cool decentralized network tech also You are aware that the resource you link was made with a site builder that mentions an AI in the second sentence of their product hero? The resource was handmade, but not far away from AI. Nice catch, but they used it before it was "AI-powered", which speaks a bit to the difficulty I'm facing trying to find alternatives to that. Yes, sloppification is everywhere. Things that were once normal products now have an AI...
